notes: Washington has no personal income tax on wages or self-employment income for tax year 2026.

ESSB 6346 (Chapter 238, Laws of 2026) enacts a 9.9% tax on Washington taxable income above a $1,000,000 per-individual standard deduction beginning January 1, 2028 (first returns/payments in 2029); it does not apply to 2026. Initiative 2111 (2024) prohibiting personal income taxes was cited in the bill report; the new tax may face legal challenge.
Washington's capital gains excise tax on long-term capital gains is not modeled (irrelevant to ordinary freelance income).

Washington instead taxes gross receipts via the business and occupation (B&O) tax; see businessCosts. The calculator models service-and-other-activities B&O at 1.5% of gross receipts (treated as a deductible business expense) with the small business B&O credit computed annually: maximum $160 x 12 = $1,920; when B&O tax exceeds that, credit = 2 x $1,920 - tax, reaching $0 at $3,840 of tax (RCW 82.04.4451; DOR credit 720 table). Monthly or quarterly filers compute the credit per period, so actual results can differ slightly. Retail sales tax and local B&O taxes are not modeled.

ESSB 5814 (effective October 1, 2025) made several services retail sales subject to sales tax and retailing B&O (not service B&O): IT services, custom software/website development, technical support, temporary staffing, advertising services, live presentations, investigation/security. Freelancers in those fields collect sales tax and pay the 0.471% retailing B&O rate instead of the service rate.

grossReceiptsTax.label: Washington B&O tax (service and other activities, 1.5%)

seDeduction.note: Not applicable: Washington has no personal income tax.

seHealthInsurance.note: Not applicable: Washington has no personal income tax.

retirementContributions.note: Not applicable: Washington has no personal income tax.

qbi.note: Not applicable: Washington has no personal income tax.

localIncomeTax.note: No local income taxes. Some cities (e.g. Seattle, Tacoma, Bellevue) impose their own local B&O taxes and business license fees, which are not modeled.

estimatedTax.threshold: None: Washington has no personal income tax, so there are no state estimated income tax payments. B&O tax is paid on the excise tax return on the filing frequency DOR assigns (annual, quarterly or monthly).
estimatedTax.form: None (B&O tax is reported on the Combined Excise Tax Return via My DOR)

businessCosts.llcFormationFee: $180 (Certificate of Formation / original filing, Washington Secretary of State); optional expedited service $100 extra. A separate Business License Application with DOR is required (processing fee varies).
businessCosts.annualReportFee: $70 per year (annual report for LLCs, Secretary of State); $95 if filed late with delinquency fee; $10 initial report.
businessCosts.franchiseOrMinimumTax: None (no franchise tax or minimum tax; no corporate or personal income tax).
businessCosts.grossReceiptsTax: Business & Occupation (B&O) tax on gross receipts. Service & Other Activities classification, effective Oct 1, 2025 (ESHB 2081, Chapter 420, Laws of 2025): 1.5% if the business (with affiliates) had less than $1,000,000 of such taxable income in the prior calendar year; 1.75% for $1,000,000 to $4,999,999.99; 2.1% for $5 million or more (hospitals and certain advanced computing businesses stay at 1.5%). Small Business B&O Credit (credit 720, for businesses with 50%+ of income under Service & Other Activities): up to $160 per month of the reporting period, phasing out dollar-for-dollar as B&O tax due rises above $160, fully gone when tax due exceeds $320/month (annual filers: credit ends above $3,840 of B&O tax; roughly the first ~$125,000 of service income is tax-free, fully phased out around $250,000). Registration/business license required if gross income is $12,000 per year or more; businesses with under $125,000 of gross income across all B&O classifications (and no retail sales tax collection or other DOR tax) may qualify for active non-reporting status. Annual filing for estimated tax liability of $1,050 or less. ESSB 6346 (2026) raises the service credit to $375/month and the annual filing threshold to $250,000 starting January 1, 2029 (not 2026).
